evals.prompt: After placing Amazon RDS Proxy in front of Aurora PostgreSQL, `DatabaseConnectionsCurrentlySessionPinned` sits at `92%` across our Node.js (`pg`), Python (`psycopg` v3), and Java (`pgjdbc`) microservices, defeating connection multiplexing. evals.expected_output: Loads `references/online-ddl-proxy-and-role-hardening.md` and explains all major RDS Proxy PostgreSQL pinning causes & fixes: (1) protocol-level / named prepared statements (`pg` `name:` field, `psycopg` `prepare_threshold` default `5` -> set `prepare_threshold=None`, `pgjdbc` `prepareThreshold` -> set `prepareThreshold=0` or `preferQueryMode=simple` where needed); (2) session-level `SET` statements (e.g., `SET search_path`, `SET timezone` -> move to RDS DB Parameter Group or RDS Proxy `InitQuery` so every backend matches without pinning); and (3) temporary tables (`CREATE TEMP TABLE`), `LISTEN/NOTIFY`, advisory locks, or >16 KB query text.
expectations: Activates the db-ha-dr-and-schema-evolution skill and loads `references/online-ddl-proxy-and-role-hardening.md`

evals.prompt: Review two resilience gaps in our Aurora PostgreSQL cluster (`1` `db.r7g.4xlarge` writer + `2` `db.r7g.large` analytics readers all at `PromotionTier = 1`, `7`-day backups in the same account): what happens if the writer fails over to a `db.r7g.large` reader, and how should we harden failover tiers and cross-account ransomware backups?

expectations: Activates the db-ha-dr-and-schema-evolution skill
Explains the undersized failover trap and configures a matching `db.r7g.4xlarge` standby at `PromotionTier = 0/1` while pinning smaller `db.r7g.large` analytics readers to `PromotionTier = 15`
Recommends cross-account / cross-region AWS Backup copies with Backup Vault Lock (Compliance mode) or Logically Air-Gapped Vaults
